svg.title: Figure 3. Strain and stress in elastic bending
svg.desc: Three panels through the depth of a beam under positive moment. (a) The strain varies linearly from compression at the top to tension at the bottom and is zero at the neutral axis. (b) The elastic stress has the same linear shape; equilibrium requires its resultant force to vanish and its moment to equal M. (c) A beam with a stiffer strip at the bottom: the strain is still linear and continuous, but the stress in the strip is n times larger at the same strain, so it jumps at the interface, and the neutral axis moves below mid-depth.
